one_line_idea: Perception heads trained on one diffusion backbone transfer to a different diffusion backbone through a single linear adapter, indicating a shared 'generative representation geometry' across independently trained models.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Every new diffusion checkpoint (versions, retrains, different labs) currently requires retraining downstream perception heads from scratch, and cross-model representational compatibility is unmeasured.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Diffusion models trained on similar data converge to representations that are equivalent up to a linear map, so frozen heads plus a cheap adapter recover most cross-model transfer performance.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] A linear adapter fit on 1% of task data will recover at least 90% of the target-backbone's native head performance for segmentation/depth probes; kill if recovery is below 70% or requires nonlinear adapters to reach it.
why_important: Linear cross-model portability would decouple perception-head investment from generator churn and constitutes evidence for a convergent-representation law in generative models.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Representational convergence is studied across discriminative networks; a head-portability protocol across generative denoisers appears untested.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Train dense-prediction heads on backbone A features, fit linear adapters from backbone B features to backbone A feature space on a small paired image set, and evaluate the frozen head on adapted features.
main_risk: Different latent VAEs between model families may break spatial alignment in ways no linear map fixes, confounding the geometry claim with tokenization mismatch.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Heads are assumed backbone-specific; nobody expects frozen heads to survive a backbone swap.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Convergence results in the literature concern coarse similarity metrics, which can be high while task-relevant fine structure remains incompatible.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Head training plus adapter fitting on public dense benchmarks across two public checkpoints is roughly 1-2 GPU-days on a single GPU.

one_line_idea: Generative pretraining specifically resolves symmetric-part ambiguity in semantic correspondence (left/right paws, wheels), predicting a large margin over discriminative features exactly on symmetry-confusable pairs and near-parity elsewhere.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Correspondence benchmarks average over all keypoint pairs, and reported diffusion-feature advantages are aggregate, leaving unexplained where the generative advantage actually comes from.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Because generation requires globally consistent part assignment (a left wheel must stay left across the image), diffusion features carry global side/orientation context that discriminative local features lack; the advantage concentrates on symmetry-confusable keypoints.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Stratifying a public correspondence benchmark into symmetry-confusable versus unambiguous keypoints will show diffusion features reducing symmetry-flip errors by at least 30% relative to a matched discriminative baseline, while unambiguous-pair accuracy differs by under 5% relative; kill if the advantage is uniform across strata.
why_important: It converts a leaderboard delta into a mechanism (global consistency from generative training), guiding when practitioners should pay diffusion-feature inference costs.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Symmetry-flip stratification of correspondence errors by pretraining objective appears unpublished.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Label symmetry-confusable keypoint pairs on an existing public benchmark, evaluate diffusion and discriminative features, and compare error decompositions.
main_risk: Symmetry-confusable subsets are small, so confidence intervals may be too wide without extra annotation effort.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Diffusion-feature correspondence gains are attributed to generally 'richer' features rather than any specific relational capability.
why_it_might_be_wrong: The gains may instead come from higher feature resolution or ensemble effects that stratification will not isolate.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Stratified re-evaluation of existing public benchmarks with two feature families is a sub-day single-GPU analysis.

one_line_idea: Generative depth estimators fine-tuned from image diffusion models inherit a photometric prior that fails predictably on non-photorealistic inputs, locating the boundary of the 'repurpose a generator' recipe.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Fine-tuning text-to-image diffusion models into dense predictors (e.g., affine-invariant depth) is an established recipe, but where its advantage comes from and where it breaks are characterized only anecdotally.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The recipe's advantage is a photometric-realism prior; on inputs violating natural image statistics (line drawings, scientific visualizations, flat-shaded renders) generative depth models will degrade more than discriminatively pretrained depth models of matched in-domain accuracy.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On a matched-pairs protocol (photo vs non-photorealistic depiction of the same geometry), generative-prior depth error will increase at least 2x more than the discriminative baseline's increase; kill if degradations are within 25% relative of each other.
why_important: Teams are adopting generator-derived dense predictors broadly; a validated failure-boundary law tells them when the prior helps versus actively misleads.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Comparisons focus on photo benchmarks; a controlled depiction-style stress protocol contrasting pretraining priors appears missing.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Assemble photo/render/drawing triplets of identical scenes from public synthetic sources with ground-truth depth, evaluate both model families, and compare degradation ratios.
main_risk: Style transfer between depiction types also changes low-level statistics that affect both families, requiring careful matched-difficulty construction.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Generative initialization is assumed to give broadly better zero-shot robustness, full stop.
why_it_might_be_wrong: The generative prior may encode geometry abstractly enough to survive depiction shifts, in which case the recipe is even stronger than believed.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Evaluation-only study on public depth checkpoints plus synthetic scenes: under one day on a single GPU.

one_line_idea: Image generators know occluded shape: diffusion features support amodal (completed-shape) segmentation probes far above discriminative features, because generation requires representing whole objects before occlusion.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Amodal completion is hard for standard perception stacks trained on visible-pixel labels, and current amodal methods rely on specialized supervision.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] To synthesize plausible occlusion scenes, generative models internally represent complete object shape; linear probes on diffusion features will predict occluded object extent substantially better than probes on discriminative features with identical heads and data.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On public amodal benchmarks, diffusion-feature probes will beat matched discriminative-feature probes by at least 8 points amodal IoU on heavily occluded instances; kill if the margin is under 3 points.
why_important: A validated amodal advantage would open a cheap route to occlusion-aware perception (robotics grasping, driving) without amodal-specific pretraining.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Diffusion features are probed for visible-region tasks; systematic amodal probing with occlusion-stratified analysis appears new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Train identical lightweight amodal-mask heads on frozen diffusion versus discriminative features using a public amodal dataset, stratify results by occlusion fraction.
main_risk: Amodal ground truth is partly annotator convention, capping measurable differences between any two feature families.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Amodal ability is assumed to require explicit amodal supervision or video; static generative pretraining is not credited with it.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Generators may handle occlusion purely at the pixel level during synthesis without maintaining reusable object-complete representations.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Frozen-feature head training on a public amodal dataset: about one day on one GPU.

one_line_idea: Diffusion-classifier accuracy is bottlenecked by noise-sample variance rather than model knowledge, so paired-noise variance reduction closes most of the gap to discriminative readouts at a fraction of the usual inference cost.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Classification via conditional diffusion likelihood estimates (diffusion classifiers) trails discriminative heads and needs many noise samples per class, which is attributed to generative models simply being worse classifiers.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The class-conditional loss differences that drive the decision are small relative to per-noise-sample variance; sharing identical noise draws across classes and antithetic sampling shrink the estimator variance enough to reveal substantially higher underlying accuracy.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Variance-reduced estimation at a fixed budget of 32 denoiser calls per image will recover at least half of the accuracy gap between a naive 32-call diffusion classifier and its 512-call ceiling; kill if the recovery is under 20% of that gap.
why_important: If the bottleneck is estimator variance, generative classifiers become practical zero-shot evaluators of what generators know, and 'generative models are bad classifiers' needs rewriting as 'naive estimators are bad'.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Paired-noise evaluation is used in some evaluation contexts; a systematic variance-decomposition study of diffusion classifiers appears missing.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Implement naive versus paired/antithetic estimators on a public text-to-image checkpoint over a class-balanced public subset, plot accuracy versus number of denoiser calls for both, and compare convergence.
main_risk: Variance reduction cannot fix systematic likelihood biases (e.g., class-dependent contour lengths), which may dominate for fine-grained classes.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] The gap is read as generative pretraining encoding less discriminative information.
why_it_might_be_wrong: If bias rather than variance dominates, the recovery will be negligible and the pessimistic reading stands.
fastest_falsification_experiment: A few thousand images with tens of denoiser calls each on one GPU: about one day with public checkpoints and data.

one_line_idea: Cross-attention localization in text-to-image models collapses selectively for relational prompts: attention maps localize single objects well but misassign attributes in two-object scenes at a rate predictable from token co-occurrence statistics.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Cross-attention maps are widely reused as free open-vocabulary localizers, but their failure structure is folklore rather than quantified.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Attention-map localization is reliable exactly when prompt tokens map to visually distinctive regions independently, and breaks when attribute binding is required, with error rate rising with training-corpus co-occurrence between the attributes and both objects.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On generated two-object scenes with swapped attributes, token-attribution maps will assign the attribute to the wrong object in at least 25% of cases while single-object localization stays above 85% pointing-game accuracy; kill if relational and single-object accuracy differ by under 10 points.
why_important: Dozens of pipelines mine attention maps for grounding; a quantified reliability boundary determines when that shortcut corrupts downstream labels.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Attribute-binding failures are known for generation quality; their signature specifically in attention-based localization appears uncharacterized.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Generate controlled two-object attribute-swap prompts, extract token attention maps, score object and attribute assignment against automatically checkable layouts, stratify by corpus co-occurrence estimates.
main_risk: Attention maps depend on layer/timestep aggregation choices, so conclusions must be shown stable across the standard extraction recipes.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Cross-attention is treated as a serviceable free localizer whose errors are unstructured noise.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Localization may fail more broadly (even single objects) once evaluated beyond cherry-picked classes, making the relational story too generous.
fastest_falsification_experiment: A few thousand controlled generations plus automated scoring: under one day on a single GPU.

one_line_idea: Occlusion ordering (which object is in front) is linearly decodable from diffusion self-attention geometry without any depth supervision, and more accurately than from discriminative features.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Pairwise occlusion-order prediction usually relies on depth estimates or supervised ordering heads; whether generative features encode ordering directly is unknown.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Synthesizing correct occlusions forces generators to represent depth ordering as an explicit relational feature, making pairwise front/behind relations linearly separable in attention-derived embeddings.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] A linear classifier on pooled pairwise attention features will predict occlusion order on public panoptic datasets with at least 80% accuracy, beating the same probe on discriminative features by 8 or more points; kill if below 70% or within 3 points of baseline.
why_important: Cheap ordering readouts would benefit scene-graph, AR insertion, and editing pipelines, and would evidence relational (not just per-pixel) scene structure inside generators.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Depth probing of diffusion features exists; explicit pairwise occlusion-order probing appears unexplored.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Derive occlusion-order pairs from public panoptic/instance annotations, pool diffusion features over instance pairs, train linear probes, compare against discriminative baselines.
main_risk: Ordering ground truth derived from annotations is noisy at contact boundaries, so instance-pair selection needs care.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Occlusion order is assumed to require metric or ordinal depth machinery rather than being a directly readable relational feature.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Apparent ordering readout may reduce to y-coordinate and size heuristics that any feature family supports equally.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Feature pooling plus linear probes on public datasets: a few hours on one GPU.

one_line_idea: Diffusion features degrade more gracefully under common corruptions than discriminative features, with a measurable crossover severity beyond which the denoising-adjacent pretraining advantage dominates.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Corruption robustness of dense predictors is usually attributed to augmentation recipes; the pretraining objective's causal role is rarely isolated.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Because denoising training continuously exposes the network to corrupted inputs, diffusion features retain task-relevant structure deeper into corruption severity, producing a severity-dependent crossover where they overtake stronger clean-condition discriminative features.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On corruption-benchmark protocols applied to frozen-feature dense probes, diffusion features' relative degradation from severity 1 to 5 will be at least 30% smaller than discriminative features', with a crossover at or before severity 4 for at least half the corruption types; kill if no crossover occurs anywhere and degradation slopes are within 10% relative.
why_important: It would give a principled reason to pay diffusion inference costs in degraded-input regimes (dashcams, drones, low light) rather than choosing backbones by clean-set leaderboards.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Robustness comparisons exist for classifiers; frozen-feature dense-probe degradation-slope comparisons across pretraining objectives appear missing.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Apply standard public corruption suites to a dense probe benchmark, evaluate frozen diffusion versus discriminative features with identical heads across severities, fit degradation slopes.
main_risk: Noise-type corruptions overlap with diffusion's training corruption, risking an unfair advantage that does not generalize to blur/weather/digital corruption families; report per-family.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Robustness is assumed to come from data scale and augmentation, with pretraining objective an afterthought.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Latent-space diffusion may lose the pixel-corruption exposure benefit since the VAE, not the denoiser, absorbs pixel noise.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Frozen-feature probing across corruption severities on public data: about one day on a single GPU.

one_line_idea: Structured inpainting is a scene-understanding test: masking context-critical regions and scoring semantic plausibility of completions yields a graded measure of what a generator understands about scenes, orthogonal to image-quality scores.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Claims that generators 'understand scenes' are argued from cherry-picked samples; the community lacks a graded, falsifiable instrument for generative scene understanding.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Completion plausibility under context-selective masking (mask the road but keep the cars; mask the shadow but keep the object) measures relational scene knowledge, and models of similar image quality will separate widely on it.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Two public generators within 10% of each other on standard quality metrics will differ by at least 25% relative on context-consistency scores (checked by off-the-shelf detectors/VQA over completions, e.g., shadow direction consistent with object and light); kill if all tested model pairs track quality metrics within 10% relative.
why_important: A capability instrument decoupled from image fidelity would let the field track scene reasoning in generators over time, the way probing suites did for language models.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Inpainting benchmarks score realism and fidelity; context-selective masking as a graded understanding probe appears unformalized.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Build a small mask taxonomy (support surfaces, shadows, reflections, contact points) over public scene images, run several public inpainting-capable models, and score completions with automated consistency checks plus a small human study.
main_risk: Automated consistency checkers have their own error rates and may cap the instrument's resolution below the differences of interest.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Scene understanding in generators is assumed to co-move with sample quality, so no separate instrument is needed.
why_it_might_be_wrong: If understanding and fidelity are in fact tightly coupled, the instrument adds measurement cost without new signal.
fastest_falsification_experiment: A few thousand masked completions across 3 public models plus automated scoring: 1-2 days on one GPU.

one_line_idea: Single-image diffusion features carry motion affordances: a linear probe predicts the plausible optical-flow direction field of a static frame, revealing implicit dynamics knowledge in image-only generators.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Image generators are trained on stills, and whether they encode anything about how scenes move is unknown; motion understanding is assumed to require video training.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Natural images betray their dynamics (poses mid-stride, water direction, traffic orientation), and generative training encodes these cues into features from which coarse expected-motion fields are linearly decodable.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] A probe from single-frame diffusion features to the next-frame flow direction (quantized to 8 bins, evaluated on public video datasets' first frames) will exceed 45% accuracy on moving pixels against a 12.5% chance floor and beat discriminative-feature probes by at least 5 points; kill if within 2 points of baseline or below 30% accuracy.
why_important: Implicit-dynamics readouts from image models would benefit video prediction initialization and would sharpen the debate about what static generative pretraining captures.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Affordance probing exists for action recognition features; motion-direction probing of image-diffusion features appears new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Take first frames plus computed flow from public videos, train linear probes from frozen features of several backbones to quantized flow direction, compare accuracies on moving regions.
main_risk: Flow direction correlates with easy cues (object class priors like cars move forward), so a class-conditional control analysis is needed to show the probe is not class lookup.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Motion knowledge is assumed absent from image-only models; video pretraining is considered necessary for any dynamics signal.
why_it_might_be_wrong: The probe may work equally well from any semantic feature via class priors, making the 'dynamics in generative features' framing an overclaim.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Probe training on precomputed flow from public video datasets: under one day on one GPU.

one_line_idea: A one-step distilled diffusion model retains most of the parent's dense-perception feature quality at 1/20th the extraction cost, making diffusion backbones cost-competitive with discriminative ViTs for the first time.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Diffusion-feature extraction requires forwarding a large denoiser (sometimes at several timesteps), which prices diffusion backbones out of most dense-prediction deployments.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Distillation to one step preserves the internal representation (which the student must keep to imitate the teacher's output map) even while trajectory information is lost, so probe performance drops far less than generation-diversity metrics do.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Frozen features from a public one-step distilled student will retain at least 90% of teacher probe performance on a fixed dense suite (segmentation, depth, correspondence); kill if retention falls below 75% on two or more tasks.
why_important: If retention holds, every diffusion-for-perception result gets a deployment path, changing the cost-benefit calculus versus discriminative backbones.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Distilled models are evaluated for generation speed/quality; their feature-space utility for perception appears unmeasured.

one_line_idea: Classifier-free guidance sharpens the output distribution with a lawful, measurable exponent: embedding-space sample variance shrinks as a power law in guidance scale, with mode-dropping onset at a critical scale predictable from conditional/unconditional score divergence.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Guidance scale is tuned by eye per model and prompt family; the community lacks a quantitative law for how guidance trades diversity for alignment.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Guidance acts as a temperature-like sharpening whose variance-reduction exponent is approximately constant across prompts within a model, and modes drop when the sharpened density's local mass falls below a threshold set by the divergence between conditional and unconditional scores.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Log embedding-variance versus log guidance scale will be linear (R^2 >= 0.9) over the practical range for at least 80% of tested prompt families, and the estimated critical scale will predict observed mode-count collapse within +/-1 guidance unit; kill if linearity fails (R^2 < 0.7) for most prompts or critical-scale predictions miss by more than 2 units.
why_important: A guidance law would replace folklore scale-tuning with prediction, and would ground diversity-alignment tradeoffs in measurable score geometry.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Guidance effects are studied qualitatively and via samples; a pre-registered variance power-law with a divergence-predicted critical point appears untested.
minimal_falsification_experiment: For fixed prompts, sample large batches across guidance scales, compute embedding-space variance and mode counts via clustering, independently estimate conditional/unconditional score divergence along trajectories, and test the predicted relationships.
main_risk: Embedding choice (which encoder) may drive the measured exponents, requiring replication across at least two unrelated embedding spaces.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Guidance is understood directionally (higher = sharper, less diverse) but treated as unlawful, prompt-specific behavior.
why_it_might_be_wrong: The sharpening may be strongly timestep-heterogeneous, so no single exponent summarizes it and the law fails as stated.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Tens of thousands of samples across scales for ~20 prompts on one GPU: roughly 1-2 days with public checkpoints.

one_line_idea: CFG's benefit is confined to a narrow mid-trajectory SNR window, and its artifacts (oversaturation, waxy textures) are produced almost entirely by applying guidance outside that window at low noise.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Guidance is conventionally applied at every step, and interval/scheduled guidance variants that restrict it are reported to help, but a mechanism-level account of where alignment benefit versus artifact harm originates along the trajectory is not settled.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Semantic alignment is decided in a mid-SNR window where conditional and unconditional scores disagree about content; at low noise the disagreement is dominated by color/contrast statistics, so late guidance mostly extrapolates off-manifold and produces the saturation artifact family.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Guidance applied only in the identified mid-SNR window will retain at least 90% of full-schedule alignment (text-image score) while reducing saturation-artifact measures by at least 50%; kill if window-only guidance loses more than 25% of the alignment gain at any window placement.
why_important: It converts a bag of scheduling tricks into a mechanistic account of guidance harm, and gives a principled default (guide where content is decided, never where palette is decided).
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Interval guidance is prior work by strong recall; the artifact-attribution decomposition (which SNR band causes which artifact family) appears unmapped.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Sweep guidance windows over SNR bands at fixed total guidance strength, measure alignment and artifact metrics (saturation statistics, clipping rates) per window, and localize benefit and harm curves.
main_risk: Alignment metrics themselves prefer saturated images, contaminating the benefit measurement; use multiple alignment measures including human checks on a subsample.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Guidance artifacts are viewed as an unavoidable tax of high scales rather than a localizable trajectory effect.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Benefit and harm may be inseparable in the same window, in which case interval guidance gains are coincidental and the decomposition fails.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Window sweeps at ~10 placements times ~2k samples on one GPU: about a day with public models.

one_line_idea: The null-prompt baseline in CFG is the wrong anchor: replacing the empty-string unconditional branch with a learned corpus-mean prompt embedding yields equal alignment at lower guidance scales with fewer artifacts.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] CFG contrasts the conditional score against an empty-prompt score, an arbitrary anchor inherited from training-time condition dropout.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The empty prompt is itself an off-distribution condition whose score has idiosyncratic biases; anchoring guidance at the corpus-mean condition produces a cleaner contrast direction, achieving the same alignment with smaller extrapolation magnitude.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Mean-anchor guidance will match null-anchor alignment at a guidance scale at least 25% lower and reduce artifact measures by at least 20% at matched alignment; kill if required scales differ by under 10% or artifacts do not improve.
why_important: A drop-in anchor change requiring no retraining that reduces guidance pathology would be immediately deployable and clarifies what the unconditional branch actually contributes.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Negative-prompt and guidance-rescaling tricks exist; a systematic study of the anchor distribution as the design variable appears missing.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Compute a mean prompt embedding from a large public caption corpus, run guidance with null versus mean anchors across scales, and compare alignment-artifact Pareto fronts.
main_risk: Models trained with empty-string dropout may treat the null condition specially, making the mean anchor off-distribution for the learned score in a different way.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] The null prompt is treated as the canonical unconditional distribution rather than one arbitrary anchor among many.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Training-time dropout may have specifically calibrated the null-prompt score as the marginal, making it exactly the right anchor and the mean embedding wrong.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Pareto sweep with two anchors, ~4k samples per configuration on one GPU: under a day using public checkpoints and caption corpora.

one_line_idea: Negative prompts and positive guidance are mechanistically asymmetric: negation via score subtraction removes appearance features but cannot remove relational or compositional content, predicting a measurable class of un-negatable concepts.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Negative prompting is a ubiquitous practitioner tool, but what kinds of content it can and cannot remove has no systematic characterization.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Score-space subtraction can suppress concepts encoded as roughly linear appearance directions (styles, textures, single objects) but fails for content encoded relationally (spatial arrangements, object counts, interactions), which lacks a subtractable direction.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] A taxonomy-based test will show appearance-level negative prompts succeeding in over 70% of generations while relational negative prompts (e.g., suppressing 'two objects touching') succeed in under 30%; kill if success rates differ by less than 15 points across the taxonomy.
why_important: It would define the operational limits of the field's main content-control lever and predict where safety-motivated negative prompting silently fails.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Negative prompting is studied as a trick; a concept-taxonomy characterization of negatability appears absent.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Build a concept taxonomy (texture/style, object, attribute, count, relation), generate with matched positive prompts plus each negative type, and score suppression success with detectors and VQA models.
main_risk: Automated suppression scoring is weakest exactly for relational content, risking measurement asymmetry that mimics the hypothesized effect; calibrate scorers on synthetic ground truth first.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Negative prompts are assumed to work uniformly, just more weakly than positive prompts.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Failures may track training-corpus frequency rather than concept type, making corpus statistics the real variable.
fastest_falsification_experiment: A few thousand generations across the taxonomy with automated scoring: under a day on one GPU.

one_line_idea: Guidance direction transfers across model scale: the conditional-minus-unconditional score direction computed by a small cheap model can steer a large model's sampling with most of the alignment benefit at a fraction of the compute.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] CFG doubles inference cost because both branches run on the full model at every step; guidance-distillation folds it into weights but freezes the scale choice.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The guidance direction is a low-complexity semantic signal that small models estimate nearly as well as large ones, so cross-model guidance (large conditional branch, small model providing the contrast) preserves alignment while cutting the second-branch cost.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Cross-scale guidance will retain at least 85% of same-model CFG's alignment gain while cutting guidance-branch FLOPs by at least 4x; kill if retention falls below 60% after affine calibration of the small model's direction.
why_important: It halves a cost every deployment pays, keeps the scale knob live (unlike distilled guidance), and tests whether guidance information is scale-invariant, a claim about what guidance is.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Related tricks exist (weak-model guidance ideas by recall); a systematic scale-transfer retention curve with calibration appears unmeasured.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Pair public checkpoints of different scales sharing conditioning interfaces, run cross-scale CFG with per-timestep affine calibration of directions, and measure alignment retention versus FLOP savings.
main_risk: Latent-space mismatch between differently trained models may require alignment machinery whose cost eats the savings.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Both branches are assumed to require the same (full) model since the contrast is between that model's own beliefs.
why_it_might_be_wrong: If guidance quality depends on fine model-specific score errors canceling between branches, a foreign contrast branch breaks the cancellation and artifacts explode.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Cross-guidance sampling sweeps on one GPU with public checkpoints of two scales: about a day.

one_line_idea: High guidance scales amplify verbatim training-set recall: for duplication-prone prompts, extraction rates rise superlinearly with guidance scale because guidance sharpens toward memorized attractors.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Memorization studies typically fix a guidance scale, and guidance studies ignore memorization, leaving the interaction unmeasured.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Memorized images act as sharp modes of the conditional density; since guidance exponentially reweights toward regions where conditional and unconditional scores disagree most, it preferentially amplifies exactly those attractors.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] For prompts with known duplicated training content, near-copy generation rate will grow superlinearly in guidance scale (at least 3x from scale 1 to scale 7), while matched non-duplicated prompts stay flat within 1.5x; kill if extraction rates are flat or sublinear in scale.
why_important: Privacy audits and deployment defaults currently pick guidance scales for aesthetics; a guidance-memorization coupling would make scale a privacy parameter.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Guidance's role as a memorization amplifier with a measured scale-response curve appears unquantified.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Identify duplication-prone prompts via public dedup analyses of open training corpora, sample across guidance scales, and measure near-copy rates against retrieved training images with perceptual matching.
main_risk: Near-copy detection thresholds partly determine the measured curve shape; report across multiple similarity thresholds.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Memorization is attributed to data duplication and model capacity, with sampling configuration assumed irrelevant.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Verbatim recall may already saturate at low scale for truly duplicated items, flattening the curve and refuting the amplifier story.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Scale sweeps for ~200 prompt candidates with perceptual retrieval against public corpus subsets: 1-2 days on one GPU.

one_line_idea: Per-prompt optimal guidance scale is predictable from prompt statistics alone (token rarity, length, specificity), enabling a trained scale-predictor that beats any fixed global scale on the alignment-diversity Pareto front.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Deployments use one global guidance scale despite folklore that different prompts want different scales; nobody has operationalized prompt-adaptive scale selection.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The optimal scale reflects how far the conditional distribution is from the marginal, which is estimable from prompt features (rarity, syntactic specificity, embedding norm), so a lightweight regressor can set scale per prompt.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] A prompt-conditioned scale predictor will dominate every fixed scale, improving alignment at matched diversity by at least 10% relative (or diversity at matched alignment by 15% relative) on held-out prompts; kill if no adaptive policy beats the best fixed scale by more than 3% relative.
why_important: A free Pareto improvement on the most-used generation knob, plus evidence that guidance demand is a measurable property of the prompt-distribution relationship.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Scheduled and interval guidance exist; prompt-feature-driven scale regression with a Pareto-dominance claim appears new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Sample a prompt corpus across scales, find per-prompt optima under a fixed alignment-diversity utility, fit and cross-validate a prompt-feature regressor, then test Pareto dominance on held-out prompts.
main_risk: Per-prompt optima may be so noisy (seed-dependent) that the regression target barely exists.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Guidance scale is treated as a model-level constant to be tuned once, not a per-input variable.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Optimal scale may depend on unobservable factors (sampler interactions, seed) that prompt features cannot capture, capping predictor value.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Scale sweeps over ~1k prompts with automated metrics on one GPU: about 2 days; the regressor itself is minutes to train.

one_line_idea: Cross-model CFG (conditional branch from model A, unconditional from model B) works if and only if the two models' score fields agree up to an affine map, giving an operational compatibility test for mixing generative models.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Practitioners occasionally mix models in guidance-like combinations (style models, refiners) with unpredictable results and no theory of when mixing is coherent.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The CFG contrast is meaningful only when both branches share a score geometry; a cheap pre-test measuring affine alignment of the two models' scores on common inputs predicts whether mixed guidance produces coherent images or artifact soup.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] An affine-alignment score computed on 500 shared noisy inputs will predict mixed-guidance output quality across model pairs with rank correlation at least 0.7; kill if correlation falls below 0.4.
why_important: A compatibility law would turn ad-hoc model mixing into an engineering discipline and illuminate how much score geometry is shared across independently trained generators.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Model soups and merged checkpoints are studied for weights; a score-field compatibility criterion for sampling-time mixing appears unformulated.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Assemble 10+ public checkpoint pairs, compute score-alignment statistics on shared inputs, run mixed guidance per pair, and correlate alignment with output quality metrics and failure rates.
main_risk: Quality of mixed outputs is multi-dimensional; a single rank correlation may hide which failure families the test misses.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Mixing models in guidance is considered a hack whose success is idiosyncratic and untestable in advance.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Compatibility may be timestep-dependent in ways a single affine test misses, requiring a more expensive trajectory-level criterion.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Score-alignment probing plus mixed sampling across ~10 model pairs on one GPU: about 2 days with public checkpoints.

one_line_idea: Perceptual guidance strength is what saturates, not information: past a modest scale, extra guidance stops adding text-relevant image content and only shifts global statistics, measurable as a plateau in mutual-information proxies between prompt tokens and image regions.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Users push guidance scales high because alignment scores keep inching upward, yet the added 'alignment' at high scales may be stylistic exaggeration rather than added content correspondence.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Token-to-region information transfer saturates at moderate guidance; beyond that point alignment-metric gains are driven by saturation/contrast statistics those metrics happen to reward, not by additional semantic binding.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Attribution-based token-region correspondence measures will plateau (slope < 10% of initial) beyond a saturation scale while global alignment scores keep rising by 15%+ over the same range; kill if correspondence measures keep growing in step with alignment scores.
why_important: It separates 'the image matches the text more' from 'the image looks more like what alignment metrics reward', directly affecting how guidance defaults are chosen.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Alignment-score criticisms exist in general, but a scale-resolved dissociation between content binding and metric gain appears unmeasured. This targets the guidance mechanism, not the metric itself.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Sweep guidance scale, measure (a) standard alignment scores and (b) token-region attribution/consistency measures via segmentation of prompted objects, and compare the two curves' saturation points.
main_risk: Attribution measures are noisy; disagreement between two attribution methods would leave the dissociation ambiguous.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Rising alignment scores at high guidance are read as genuinely better prompt following.
why_it_might_be_wrong: High guidance may truly continue adding content fidelity for complex prompts, with plateaus appearing only for simple ones.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Scale sweeps with two measurement families over ~1k prompts: about a day on one GPU with public models.

one_line_idea: DDIM inversion error is spectrally lawful: reconstruction error concentrates where local high-frequency energy is high, so a cheap spectral map of an image predicts where subsequent edits will fail before any editing is attempted.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Inversion-based editing fails unpredictably on some images and regions; failures are discovered only after running the full edit pipeline.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Inversion error is dominated by the ODE discretization interacting with high-curvature score regions, which co-locate with high local spectral energy; therefore a per-region spectral statistic predicts per-region inversion and editing error.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Local spectral energy will predict per-patch inversion reconstruction error with rank correlation at least 0.6 across a diverse public image set, and patches in the top spectral decile will show at least 3x the edit-failure rate of the bottom decile; kill if correlation is below 0.3.
why_important: A pre-edit failure predictor turns editing from trial-and-error into a triaged pipeline and gives a mechanistic account of which image content resists inversion.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Inversion error is reported as image-level averages; a spatially resolved spectral law with predictive use appears absent.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Invert and reconstruct a diverse public image set, compute per-patch reconstruction error and local spectral statistics, fit and cross-validate the predictor, then verify on an editing task that predicted-bad regions fail more.
main_risk: Latent-space models complicate the story since the VAE contributes its own spatially varying error, requiring a decode-only control.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Inversion failures are attributed loosely to 'hard images' or CFG mismatch, without a spatial or spectral structure claim.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Error may be dominated by global trajectory drift that no local statistic predicts, making the spatial map uninformative.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Inversion plus analysis over ~2k public images on one GPU: a few hours.

one_line_idea: Inversion failure under classifier-free guidance is a per-timestep bias, not noise: the error grows systematically with guidance scale, and null-text-style fixes work precisely because they absorb this bias term, which can be measured and corrected directly.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Inversion is derived for the unguided ODE; running edits at guidance scale w>1 breaks reconstruction, and per-image optimization tricks (null-text embedding tuning) repair it at significant cost, without a quantitative account of what is being repaired.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The guided reverse trajectory deviates from the inverted trajectory by a structured per-timestep offset dominated by the guidance term; this offset is low-dimensional and predictable, so a closed-form or cheaply fitted correction recovers most of what per-image optimization does.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] A globally fitted per-timestep correction (no per-image optimization) will recover at least 70% of the reconstruction-quality gap between naive guided inversion and per-image null-text optimization; kill if recovery is below 40%.
why_important: Editing pipelines pay minutes of per-image optimization for what may be a fixed correctable bias; the decomposition also explains a widely used but poorly understood fix.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Null-text inversion is established prior work by recall; the claim that its benefit is a globally shared, cheaply transferable bias term is untested.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Measure trajectory offsets between inversion and guided regeneration across images, test offset predictability across images (low-rank structure), fit a global correction, and benchmark against per-image optimization for reconstruction and edit quality.
main_risk: The offset may be strongly image-dependent, in which case the global correction fails and per-image optimization is genuinely necessary.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Guided-inversion failure is treated as an unavoidable inconsistency requiring per-image optimization to patch.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Guidance interacts with content multiplicatively, so a shared additive correction may be the wrong functional form entirely.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Offset measurement and global-correction fitting over ~500 images: under a day on one GPU with public checkpoints.

one_line_idea: Iterated invert-edit cycles converge to model-typical attractor images: identity drifts toward the generator's mean style at a measurable geometric rate, giving a quantitative 'regression to the generative mean' law for sequential editing.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Users report faces and objects becoming 'more generic' after repeated edits, but sequential-edit degradation has no quantitative characterization.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Each invert-edit round trip contracts the image toward high-density regions of the model distribution; identity distance to the original grows with round count following a contraction-mapping pattern with a model-specific rate.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Identity similarity to the original (face-embedding or perceptual metric) will decay approximately geometrically over 10 edit rounds with a stable fitted rate (per-model variance under 20%), and repeated no-op edits will drift measurably (at least 30% of the drift of real edits), proving the pipeline itself contracts; kill if drift is negligible for no-op edits and non-monotonic for real edits.
why_important: It defines the usable depth of sequential editing workflows, and the contraction rate is a new, meaningful model property (manifold attraction strength).
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Single-edit fidelity is benchmarked; multi-round drift dynamics with a fitted contraction law appear unstudied.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Run 10 rounds of no-op and mild edits over a diverse image set across two editors, track identity metrics per round, fit decay curves, and compare rates across models and edit types.
main_risk: Identity metrics saturate or become unreliable far from the natural-image manifold, so late-round measurements need multiple metric families.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Edit degradation is blamed on individual edit operations rather than a systematic attractor dynamic of the invert-regenerate loop.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Drift may be a random walk (variance growth without directional pull), which the no-op control would reveal as non-contractive.
fastest_falsification_experiment: 10-round loops on ~300 images for two public editors: about a day on one GPU.

one_line_idea: The inversion-error gap between model-generated and real photographs of matched content is a quantitative measure of the generator's manifold mismatch, usable as a model-diagnostic that tracks training data coverage.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Generated images invert almost perfectly while real photos do not, but this asymmetry is treated as a nuisance rather than measured as a property of the model.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The real-vs-generated inversion-error gap, computed over content-matched pairs, measures how far the model's learned manifold sits from the real data manifold in each content category, and it varies lawfully across categories with training-data density.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] The per-category inversion gap will correlate with independent estimates of category frequency in the training corpus at rank correlation 0.5 or better across 30+ categories; kill if correlation is under 0.25.
why_important: A cheap post-hoc probe of where a generator's manifold is thin would guide data curation and flag categories where editing and perception uses of the model will fail.

why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Basin-of-attraction analysis of memorized modes in diffusion score fields appears unexplored; existing detection heuristics are output-side.

main_risk: Sharpness varies with content complexity generally (flat regions converge fast), so controls must match content statistics, not just class.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Memorization is treated as a data/duplication problem, without commitments about local geometry of the learned score field.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Memorized items may be reached through ordinary-width basins whose distinguishing property is location, not sharpness, nullifying the geometric signature.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Perturbation ensembles for ~100 memorized plus 100 control items: a few hours on one GPU.

why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Sampler comparisons focus on speed-quality; a controlled paired spectral analysis attributing texture to stochasticity appears missing.

one_line_idea: A model's quality-versus-steps exponent predicts its distillability: generators whose sample quality converges fast in step count distill to few-step students with less loss, giving a cheap pre-test before paying distillation compute.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Distillation outcomes vary across base models for unclear reasons, and teams discover failures only after expensive distillation runs.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Both step-count convergence and distillability are governed by the curvature of the model's probability-flow ODE: low-curvature models need fewer steps and are easier to compress into few-step students, so the convergence exponent is a proxy for distillation loss.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Across 6+ public base models, the fitted quality-versus-NFE exponent will predict few-step distillation quality loss with rank correlation at least 0.6; kill if correlation is under 0.3.
why_important: A pre-distillation test would save large compute budgets and tie two practical properties to one geometric cause (trajectory curvature), unifying sampling and distillation science.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Step-quality curves and distillation results both exist per model; their cross-model correlation as a predictive law appears untested.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Fit quality-versus-steps exponents for a set of public checkpoints, distill each with a fixed consistency-style recipe at small scale, and correlate exponents with student quality loss.
main_risk: Distillation recipes interact with architectures; a single recipe may disadvantage some models and contaminate the correlation.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Distillability is treated as recipe-dependent trial and error with no known model-side predictor.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Distillation loss may be dominated by capacity and data factors orthogonal to trajectory curvature.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Exponent fitting is hours; the small-scale distillation grid is the bottleneck at roughly 6-10 GPU-days total on a single GPU.

one_line_idea: Popular samplers do not sample the same distribution: at convergence-equivalent settings, different sampler families produce distributionally distinct outputs (hue, contrast, composition statistics), so sampler choice silently changes every downstream measurement.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Model evaluations and comparisons freely mix sampler configurations, assuming samplers are unbiased estimators of one model distribution.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Discretization biases differ by sampler family and persist at practical step counts, producing measurable distribution-level differences (not just per-image noise) that exceed evaluation error bars.

why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Sampler artifacts are known qualitatively; a two-sample distributional-equality audit at matched compute appears missing. The target is the sampling procedure, not any evaluation metric.

main_risk: Two-sample classifiers can latch onto trivial artifacts (JPEG-level differences); control the output pipeline bit-exactly.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Sampler families are assumed to agree at convergence for all practical purposes.
why_it_might_be_wrong: At high step counts differences may truly vanish below detection, confining the effect to fast-sampling regimes only.
fastest_falsification_experiment: ~60k generations plus classifier tests: about a day on one GPU.

one_line_idea: Score-field curvature concentrates in a narrow SNR band, and allocating steps adaptively to that band beats hand-tuned schedules at matched compute, turning schedule design into a measurable-quantity optimization.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Step schedules (where to place sampling steps in noise level) are hand-crafted per model family, with folklore defaults inherited across codebases.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Local truncation error is dominated by trajectory curvature, which is empirically concentrated in a measurable SNR band; measuring curvature once per model and placing steps by curvature mass dominates generic schedules.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Curvature-adaptive schedules will match default-schedule quality with at least 25% fewer steps (or improve quality metrics by 10%+ relative at matched steps) across two models; kill if gains are under 5% relative everywhere.
why_important: A measurement-driven scheduler removes a tuning dimension for every deployment and confirms curvature as the operative quantity in sampling efficiency.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Adaptive ODE solvers exist generically; a per-model curvature-census-driven static schedule with pre-registered margins appears untested in the diffusion setting.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Estimate trajectory curvature along noise levels on a sample of generations, build the curvature-mass schedule, and benchmark against default schedules at matched NFE on standard quality metrics.
main_risk: Curvature estimates from finite differences are noisy and prompt-dependent; aggregate schedules may miss per-prompt heterogeneity that adaptive solvers capture.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Schedules are treated as inherited defaults; step placement is assumed to matter less than step count.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Modern high-order samplers may already absorb curvature effects, leaving little for schedule placement to reclaim.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Curvature census plus schedule benchmark: under a day on one GPU per model.

one_line_idea: The initial noise seed is a composition genome: under deterministic sampling, seeds impose transferable coarse layouts across prompts, and the seed-layout map is stable enough to build a searchable layout library with no model modification.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Seed effects are folklore (users keep 'good seeds'), but the information content of initial noise regarding layout is unquantified.

falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Same-seed cross-prompt layout similarity (detection-graph overlap) will exceed different-seed similarity by at least 2x on average across prompt families, and a seed library will let users hit target coarse layouts in top-5 retrieval at 60%+ success; kill if same-seed similarity exceeds baseline by under 1.2x.
why_important: Training-free layout control through seed selection would be immediately usable, and the result quantifies how labor is divided between noise and conditioning in content creation.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Seed-layout anecdotes abound; a quantified cross-prompt transfer coefficient and retrieval-based control protocol appear unpublished.

main_risk: Layout similarity metrics must ignore appearance; detector-based graphs may be too coarse for compositional nuance.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Seeds are assumed to matter, but layout is credited mostly to the prompt and model, with seed effects viewed as unstructured luck.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Prompt semantics may dominate composition for content-heavy prompts, restricting seed control to backgrounds and framing.
fastest_falsification_experiment: A 100-seed x 50-prompt grid: a few hours on one GPU.

one_line_idea: Early-stopping the reverse ODE at a nonzero noise floor is an implicit truncation trick for diffusion: it trades diversity for typicality along a lawful curve, giving a free post-hoc knob equivalent to GAN truncation with a measurable exponent.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] GANs had the truncation trick as a standard diversity-fidelity knob; diffusion deployments lack an equivalent cheap post-hoc control and instead re-tune guidance.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Terminating sampling early (then doing a final x0-prediction) contracts outputs toward high-density regions, producing a diversity-typicality tradeoff curve with a stable exponent that complements guidance and composes with it predictably.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Sweeping the stop floor will trace a smooth diversity-typicality frontier where log-diversity declines approximately linearly with stop-level (R^2 >= 0.85), and combining moderate early stop with lower guidance will match the alignment of high guidance with at least 10% relative more diversity; kill if the frontier is non-monotonic or the combination never beats guidance-only.
why_important: A second, orthogonal knob for the diversity-fidelity tradeoff would immediately improve deployment Pareto fronts and clarify the relationship between guidance and density contraction.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Early stopping is used for speed; its systematic use as a truncation-equivalent quality knob with measured exponents appears unexplored.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Sweep stop floors and guidance jointly, measure diversity (embedding dispersion) and typicality/alignment metrics, and map the two-knob Pareto surface on public models.
main_risk: The final x0-jump from a high stop floor may introduce artifact families that quality metrics misread as typicality.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Guidance is treated as the only practical diversity-fidelity knob at inference time.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Early-stop contraction may be negligible below floors that visibly blur outputs, leaving no useful operating range.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Two-knob sweep with ~10k generations: about a day on one GPU.

one_line_idea: Sample spread of generative depth models localizes at genuinely ill-posed pixels: multi-sample dispersion concentrates at occlusion boundaries and scale-ambiguous regions, matching multi-sensor disagreement rather than being uniform noise.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Diffusion-based dense predictors produce different outputs per sample, and this variability is treated either as a nuisance to average away or naively as an uncertainty estimate, without validation against the true ambiguity structure of the task.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Because the generative prior learns the multi-modality of the depth-given-image relationship, per-pixel sample dispersion is not isotropic noise but tracks the physically ill-posed structure: it peaks where the inverse problem genuinely admits multiple answers.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Per-pixel sample dispersion will rank-correlate with independent ambiguity ground truth (multi-sensor disagreement or multi-annotator variance on public RGB-D data) at 0.5+ within images, at least 2x the correlation achieved by a softmax-entropy baseline from a matched discriminative model; kill if within-image correlation is below 0.25 or no better than the discriminative baseline.
why_important: If dispersion is real ambiguity structure, generative dense predictors provide task-posterior information no point-estimate model has, changing how ambiguity should be handled in geometry pipelines.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Generative depth papers average samples for accuracy; validating dispersion against physical ambiguity ground truth appears undone.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Sample generative depth predictions many times per image on public RGB-D benchmarks with multi-sensor or multi-view-verified ground truth, compute per-pixel dispersion maps, and correlate against measured ambiguity proxies with discriminative-entropy controls.
main_risk: Ambiguity ground truth from sensor disagreement includes sensor-specific noise that is not scene ambiguity, diluting the correlation ceiling.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Sample-to-sample variation in generative predictors is treated as stochastic nuisance to be averaged for a better point estimate.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Dispersion may mostly reflect sampler stochasticity and seed sensitivity, spatially uncorrelated with true ill-posedness.
fastest_falsification_experiment: 32 samples per image over ~500 public RGB-D images plus correlation analysis: a few hours on one GPU.

one_line_idea: Generative segmentation samplers reproduce the distribution of human annotator disagreement, not just its magnitude: sampled mask sets match inter-annotator mask distributions on multi-rater datasets better than any softmax-derived baseline.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Multi-rater datasets show humans legitimately disagree on mask boundaries and structure inclusion, yet standard models output one mask plus per-pixel scores that cannot represent structured alternatives (whole-region include/exclude choices).
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Diffusion mask samplers learn the joint structure of plausible annotations, so their sample sets capture correlated, region-level disagreement modes that per-pixel independence assumptions cannot express.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On public multi-rater segmentation data, the generalized energy distance between sampled mask sets and rater mask sets will beat per-pixel-independent baselines by at least 20% relative, specifically on region-level disagreement cases; kill if the improvement is under 5% relative or confined to boundary-width effects.
why_important: Matching the structure of expert disagreement is the requirement for downstream decision systems (e.g., review triage) that consume alternative hypotheses rather than heat maps.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Stochastic segmentation networks exist as prior work by recall; a diffusion-sampler evaluation focused on structured (region-level) versus boundary-level disagreement decomposition appears new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Train or adapt a diffusion mask sampler on a public multi-rater dataset, decompose disagreement into boundary-band versus region-inclusion components, and compare distribution-matching metrics per component against independence baselines.
main_risk: Multi-rater datasets are few and small; conclusions may be domain-narrow (largely medical), and rater pools may under-sample the true annotation distribution.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Per-pixel probability maps are assumed to summarize annotation ambiguity adequately for practical purposes.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Diffusion samplers may mode-collapse to the majority annotation style, matching magnitude but not structure, exactly like the baselines.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Adaptation plus evaluation on one public multi-rater dataset: roughly 1-2 GPU-days on a single GPU.

one_line_idea: Diffusion posterior samplers for inverse problems systematically under-disperse: sampled posteriors are provably narrower than the true posterior in controlled linear inverse settings, with a measurable contraction factor that practitioners should correct for.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Diffusion models are widely used as priors for inverse problems (deconvolution, inpainting, tomography-style tasks), and the sampled variability is presented as posterior uncertainty without validation against ground-truth posteriors.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Approximations in posterior-guidance methods (likelihood linearization, score errors, mode-seeking dynamics) compound into systematic over-concentration: the sampled posterior's variance underestimates the true posterior variance by a large, quantifiable factor that grows with measurement sparsity.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] In synthetic linear inverse problems where the exact posterior is computable (Gaussian mixtures, small images), diffusion posterior samplers will exhibit variance ratios (sampled/true) below 0.5 in sparse-measurement regimes, worsening as measurements decrease; kill if variance ratios stay within [0.8, 1.2] across regimes.
why_important: Under-dispersed posteriors mean silently overconfident scientific and medical reconstructions wherever diffusion priors are deployed; a measured contraction factor enables correction or honest reporting.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Individual guidance approximations are acknowledged in methods papers; a controlled ground-truth-posterior audit quantifying contraction appears rare or absent.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Construct linear inverse problems with analytically known posteriors using a diffusion prior trained on synthetic distributions, run standard posterior-sampling methods, and compare sampled moments and coverage against exact values across measurement counts.
main_risk: Conclusions from synthetic distributions may not transfer to natural-image priors, though the mechanism (guidance approximation) is shared.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Diffusion posterior samples are treated as approximately calibrated draws from the Bayes posterior for practical purposes.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Contraction may be method-specific rather than universal, with some guidance schemes over-dispersing instead, which the audit would also establish.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Small synthetic diffusion prior plus exact-posterior comparisons: about 1 GPU-day on a single GPU, all synthetic public-reproducible data.

one_line_idea: Distilling a generative dense predictor into a one-step model destroys ambiguity information in a predictable spatial pattern: the student blurs exactly where the teacher's samples disperse, converting represented multi-modality into averaged error.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Few-step distillation is being applied to generative dense predictors for deployment speed, evaluated by average accuracy which cannot see what happens to represented ambiguity.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Distillation objectives implicitly average over teacher modes; at pixels where the teacher's posterior is multi-modal the student regresses to the mean, so student blur/error maps will spatially match teacher dispersion maps.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Spatial correlation between teacher sample-dispersion maps and student residual-blur maps will exceed 0.5 across public depth benchmarks, and student error at high-dispersion pixels will exceed teacher single-sample error by 30%+ relative; kill if correlation is under 0.2.
why_important: It identifies a lawful information loss in the standard deployment path and motivates mixture-aware distillation, with direct consequences for any downstream consumer of ambiguity.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Distillation quality is tracked by averages; the spatial mode-collapse fingerprint linking teacher dispersion to student blur appears unexamined.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Distill a public generative depth model with a standard recipe, compute teacher dispersion and student residual maps on benchmark images, and measure spatial correspondence and stratified errors.
main_risk: Student blur also arises from capacity limits unrelated to multi-modality; a unimodal-region control comparison is required for attribution.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Distillation is assumed to preserve 'the useful part' of the teacher, with sample diversity dismissed as disposable stochasticity.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Students may commit to a single mode rather than average, in which case error concentrates differently (mode-picking) and the blur fingerprint fails.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Small-scale distillation plus map comparison: roughly 2 GPU-days on a single GPU with public models and data.

one_line_idea: The learned generative prior dominates conditioning evidence at a lawful, measurable noise threshold: for conditional dense prediction, prior-driven hallucination onsets where the condition's information rate falls below the prior's, predicting exactly where generative predictors invent content.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Conditional generative predictors hallucinate plausible-but-wrong content in weakly constrained regions, and practitioners lack any quantitative rule for when outputs stop reflecting the input.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Along the sampling trajectory there is a per-region crossover between evidence-dominated and prior-dominated dynamics, measurable by comparing output sensitivity to input perturbations against sensitivity to prior perturbations; hallucination localizes past the crossover.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] A sensitivity-ratio map (input-sensitivity over prior-sensitivity) will predict hallucination locations (regions where output disagrees with masked-input ground truth) with AUC 0.75+ across occlusion levels; kill if AUC is under 0.6.
why_important: A predictive hallucination map turns an unquantified trust problem into a per-pixel budget, essential wherever generative predictors touch measurement-critical applications.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Hallucination in conditional generation is widely noted; an evidence-versus-prior sensitivity decomposition with predictive validation appears new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: On masked dense-prediction tasks with known ground truth, compute per-region input-perturbation and prior-perturbation (seed/trajectory) sensitivities, form ratio maps, and validate against actual error locations across masking levels.
main_risk: Sensitivity estimation needs many forward passes per image; approximations may degrade the map faster than the hypothesis fails.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Hallucination is treated as an unpredictable generative vice to be handled by disclaimers or output filtering.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Hallucination may be decided globally (image-level mode choice) rather than by local evidence balance, defeating per-region prediction.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Sensitivity mapping on ~200 masked images: about a day on one GPU.

one_line_idea: Consensus across diffusion samples predicts correctness in-domain but the coupling collapses under domain shift in a measurable way, defining the validity boundary for using sample agreement as a quality proxy.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Practitioners increasingly use multi-sample agreement from generative predictors as a label-free quality signal, implicitly assuming the agreement-accuracy link is stable across conditions.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Agreement-accuracy coupling is a property of the training distribution: under distribution shift the model can be confidently wrong in correlated ways across samples, so consensus stays high while accuracy falls, breaking the proxy exactly when it is most needed.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Across a shift ladder (same task, increasing domain distance), the consensus-accuracy rank correlation will fall from 0.6+ in-domain to under 0.2 at strong shift while mean consensus itself drops by less than 20%, demonstrating correlated confident errors; kill if the coupling stays above 0.5 at all shift levels (proxy robust) or consensus collapses in step with accuracy (proxy honestly uncertain).
why_important: It establishes when agreement-based quality control is trustworthy, replacing an unexamined assumption with a measured operating envelope. The claim targets the generative sampler's error correlation structure, not any specific detector trick.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Ensemble-agreement failure under shift is studied for classifier ensembles; the within-model sampling-consensus version for generative dense predictors appears unmeasured.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Build a shift ladder from public datasets for one dense task, sample the generative predictor at each level, and track consensus statistics against accuracy with matched evaluation.
main_risk: Domain-distance ordering is partly arbitrary; use several independent shift axes (sensor, geography, style) to show the collapse is general.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Multi-sample agreement is treated as a domain-general quality signal because samples 'independently' explore the posterior.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Samples share every weight and most computation, so their errors were never independent; in-domain success may be the coincidence, not the shift failure.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Sampling across 4 shift levels x 300 images: a few hours on one GPU with public datasets.

one_line_idea: Generative amodal completion samples span the space of human beliefs about hidden content: the diversity of sampled completions for occluded regions matches the distribution of human guesses, making generators measurable models of shared visual expectation.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] What is behind an occluder is often genuinely uncertain, humans hold structured distributions over the possibilities, and no standard evaluation asks whether generative completion diversity matches human expectation distributions.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Generative models trained on natural scenes internalize the same statistical regularities humans use, so their completion distributions (object identity, extent, pose behind occluders) will approximate aggregated human predictions well beyond chance and beyond class-prior baselines.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On a curated occlusion set with collected human completion judgments, the Jensen-Shannon divergence between model completion distributions and human distributions will beat a class-prior baseline by 30%+ relative and correlate with human entropy per item at 0.4+; kill if the model matches humans no better than the class-prior baseline.
why_important: Alignment of generative imagination with human expectation is exactly what applications like occlusion-aware editing and simulation need, and it operationalizes 'models share our scene priors' as a measurable claim.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Amodal benchmarks score single-answer accuracy; distribution-level comparison against human belief distributions appears novel.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Curate occlusion images, collect multi-annotator guesses about hidden content (small human study), sample model completions, classify both into comparable category/pose bins, and compare distributions per item.
main_risk: Requires a human-judgment collection (~hundreds of items x tens of raters), which is cheap in cost but adds study logistics beyond pure compute.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Completion quality is judged by plausibility of single samples, assuming diversity is aesthetic variation rather than belief structure.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Model diversity may be dominated by texture/style variation within one hypothesis rather than genuine alternative-content hypotheses, mismatching the human distribution's structure.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Sampling and binning are a few GPU-hours; the bottleneck is a small crowd study (needs_special_resources=true only if human study is unavailable; a pilot with lab annotators suffices).
